title: Put it together: named sub-plans
idea: LOOP: mix recall - naming jobs, define vs use, honest names, design helpers. No code.

exercises.prompt: A named sub-plan (a reusable job with a name) is called a...
exercises.explanation: A function is a named sub-plan. This unit built the idea; next unit writes it as code.

options: set the job up once, then use its name as often as needed
exercises.explanation: Describe the job once; use its name repeatedly. That reuse is the main payoff of naming a job.

exercises.prompt: Defining a sub-plan makes its steps happen right away.
exercises.explanation: No. Defining only describes the job. The steps happen when you USE it. Define vs use are different.

exercises.prompt: Plan: define greet (shows 'Hi'), then use greet twice. What appears?
exercises.explanation: The define is quiet setup. Two uses show 'Hi' twice. Output follows the uses, in order.

exercises.prompt: Which jobs are worth naming as helpers? (Pick all.)
options: a border used top and bottom
totalling a basket reused per customer
exercises.explanation: Repeated or reused jobs earn names. A one-off single print usually stays inline.

exercises.prompt: Match each idea to its meaning.
exercises.explanation: Define describes, use does, and an honest name tells the truth about the job. The core ideas of this unit.

exercises.prompt: A job named 'show_score' that really prints a border is a problem because...
options: the name lies about what the job does
exercises.explanation: Misleading names cause bugs. A helper's name must honestly describe its job.

exercises.prompt: Order a short main plan: greet, total the basket, print the receipt.
exercises.explanation: greet, total_basket, print_receipt - the main plan is just named helpers in order.

exercises.prompt: A main plan built from named helpers reads like a short summary of the task.
exercises.explanation: Yes. The main plan lists the big steps by name; each helper hides its own details. Short and clear.

exercises.prompt: You've built the IDEA of a named sub-plan. What's next in the lap?
options: writing a real sub-plan and running it - define vs run in code
exercises.explanation: Next unit: the real syntax to define a sub-plan and to call it. The idea you learned becomes runnable code!
